title: Scaffold kits: portable LLM app recipes (Next.js, FastAPI, Go, CLI)
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Produce a compact set of production-oriented scaffold kits showing idiomatic usage of Redwood SDKs in Next.js (Edge & Server), FastAPI (async), Go HTTP servers, and a small CLI tool. Focus areas: reliable retries with idempotency tokens, ergonomic streaming consumption (cancellation/backpressure/resume), and copy-paste starter snippets developers can drop into real apps.
acceptance_criteria: Four scaffold projects (Next.js app, FastAPI app, Go http server, CLI) with README and working examples
Streaming examples show client cancellation, reconnect/resume semantics, and SSE/streaming adapters
Retry patterns documented and implemented (exponential backoff, idempotency token example, retry budgets)
Each example includes tests or a smoke script and links to a minimal deployment guide
PRs merged for SDK helper utilities used by examples (streaming helpers, retry helper)
tasks: Draft Next.js example demonstrating server-side streaming and edge handler fallback
Implement FastAPI async generator example with reconnectable stream and KV prefix caching demo
Build Go HTTP example with context cancellation and graceful shutdown hooks
Create CLI example (Go or Python) with resumable downloads and progress UI for streamed tokens
Write README cookbook notes covering trade-offs (latency vs batching vs cost)
Add tests, CI smoke scripts, and example app Dockerfile for local testing
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Raman: Kickoff - scoped to 4 lightweight apps and accompanying SDK helpers. Initial design doc linked.
2025-02-14 Carlos Vega: Decided to implement idempotency token examples in both HTTP request header and SDK helper to show patterns for retries across languages.

2025-02-20 Carlos Vega: Prototype FastAPI async generator working. Verified reconnect+resume using a sequence checkpoint token in the request metadata. Added notes about KV prefix caching interaction.
2025-02-24 QA: Found an issue with SSE buffer flushing in Next.js Edge runtime; temporary workaround to stream small batches. Filed follow-up task ENG-277889.
2025-02-28 Aisha Raman: Design review - prefer explicit cancel tokens via context rather than relying on connection close; added example patterns for both approaches.
2025-03-03 Carlos Vega: Opened PR #834-docs with README drafts and sample commands. Need review from SDK team for streaming helper API names.
2025-03-05 Design review: UX sign-off on README organization. Moved some advanced topics to 'advanced-recipes.md' to keep starter kits small and approachable.
notes: Prefer minimal dependencies so examples can run in CI quickly (<= 2 min start time)
Edge runtime SSE in Next.js requires small chunk flush heuristic: flush every ~512 bytes or on newline
For retries, show using an idempotency header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key' and an SDK convenience wrapper
Streaming helper API will include: on_token(callback), cancel(), resume(checkpoint)
Demonstrate how prefix KV caching reduces token billing for repeated prompts in the FastAPI example
risks: Edge runtime differences across hosting providers may break SSE behavior; include clear notes and tests
Reconnection/resume semantics depend on application-level checkpointing; risk of confusing example if not documented well
API surface for streaming helpers could change during SDK refactor; examples must be easy to update
